# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2 (15W, magnetic)**
- Qi2 is the open wireless charging standard from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). It added a magnetic ring that aligns the phone and charger, which improves efficiency and speed. Qi2 tops out at 15W. ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/))
- Apple contributed MagSafe technology to the standard. ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey))

**Qi2.2 (25W, magnetic)**
- Qi2.2 is the newer version of Qi2. The WPC brands it "Qi2 25W," and it delivers nearly 70% more power than Qi2. The WPC says it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes. ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/))
- Products were first certified in July 2025. ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey))
- Your phone has to support 25W too (see below).

**MagSafe (Apple's brand)**
- MagSafe is Apple's magnetic charging system, used on iPhone 12 and later (except the SE and 16e). ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html))
- Apple-certified MagSafe chargers deliver 15W to most iPhones and up to 25W to newer ones. ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html))
- Apple's current MagSafe Charger is itself certified for Qi2 25W. ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m))
- Certified MagSafe chargers also have an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, and a magnetometer to prevent compass interference. ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html))
- Be careful with "MagSafe-compatible" on a box. Uncertified chargers with a magnet ring are usually only 7.5W. ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html))

**What speed your iPhone gets (with a 25W-capable charger and a 30W+ adapter)**

| iPhone | Max wireless speed |
|---|---|
| iPhone 17, 17 Pro/Pro Max, 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max (and the 18 Pro models) | 25W |
| iPhone 16 and 16 Pro | 22.5W |
| iPhone Air | 20W |
| iPhone 17e, iPhone 15 and earlier | 15W |

Source: [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047). The iPhone 16e has no magnets and charges with standard Qi only.

**Android**
- Few phones support Qi2. The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold get 15W, and the Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at up to 25W. ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks))
- Samsung's Galaxy S26 series is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case to get Qi2 speeds, up to 15W. ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks))

**Which to buy**
- Chargers are backward and forward compatible, so a Qi2.2 (25W) charger works with Qi2 and MagSafe phones at their own top speed.
- A Qi2.2 or MagSafe 25W charger is only worth it for a recent iPhone (16 or newer) or a Pixel 10 Pro XL. For older phones, a 15W Qi2 charger is just as fast.
- Apple's own option is the [MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m). The 2 m version is $49 and Macworld lists the 1 m at $39. It doesn't include a power adapter, so you need a 30W+ one for full 25W speed.
